speaker: Unknown
quote_text: Thank you, Joe. Congratulations. The winning  moment. How did it feel to be a Test match-winning captain of England again? Felt good. I think  it’s been a brilliant performance from the very first ball. I think, having won the toss, we  got the chance to exploit those conditions early, and the way that we did that from the outset was  excellent. Recognising what was going to be really hard for them and rolling that out for a long  period of time was exactly what you’re after. Once we got ahead of the game, I thought we managed  it really well. We had a really good tempo with the bat. We managed to apply pressure when we got  our opportunities. There were small periods where we had to soak things up in different moments  and different partnerships. But to get 400 on there, there was obviously a lot of runs, and  we were clinical again today with the ball. So, a really pleasing start to the series and it sets  things up nicely for us. In all three disciplines, did you sense there was a calmness around the  team? It felt like that. Felt like that, yeah, especially with the nature of the lead-in to  things. The fact that we’d come straight from The Hundred, guys coming in from [inaudible],  from different kinds of cricket and having a short amount of time together, but the fact that  we very quickly got on task showed, I guess, the clarity that we had leading in, or the use  of the time that we had together as a team. We got it pretty right, and then to deliver on that  showed the skill level and the quality that we have within the team. The bowling group, I don’t  really think they understand how good they are, how well they complement each other and, in these  conditions, what they’re capable of doing. So it’s really nice for them to see that and to start the  series like that. Clearly, we’ll have different challenges and different surfaces to manage, but  it’s a brilliant start to things and I’m really pleased for all the guys. The two lads coming in  with the bat as well, Jordan and Dan, I thought they played brilliantly. Jordan at three looked  very calm, very composed and very comfortable within his own game in those conditions. Great  to see and great to bat with. Dan as well, the way he dovetailed with Brookie and played in  his own way was brilliant. So, a lot of really good stuff to take on. Obviously, in your first  go-around as captain, you had Jimmy and Stuart doing a lot of the heavy lifting for you with the  ball. Do you look at the complementary skills in that attack, and does it look like one that can  go all around the world and do the job for you? I think it’s just not getting too carried away.  I think we understand where we currently sit. What’s really important is, when we get  to Lord’s, looking at the conditions, how we’re going to exploit them, how they’re  going to complement each other, and going from there and slowly building something collectively  over time. Throughout the game, different bowlers were threatening at different times. I think the  fact that they recognised that, worked together as a partnership and were constantly communicating  what was working and how they were going to help each other out was a great start to things. A lot  of really good stuff. Those guys came into Test cricket, pretty much all of them, with two of the  most experienced bowlers we’ve ever had in Chris Woakes and Ben Stokes. That’s a lot of wickets and  a lot of seniority. So all of a sudden, you’ve got an opportunity to lead things yourselves, do  things slightly differently and step into a different space. That’s the chance they have. I  think it’s a great start to things this week in doing that. Just lastly for me, to take you out of  the moment for a second, with some of the success you’ve had here at Headingley and it being your  home ground, is there any disappointment from you that we won’t be back here next summer for an  Ashes Test? Yeah, I’d love to play as many games as possible here. I think it’s a great Test match  venue. It’s a surface that provides brilliant Test cricket and one that we’ve had quite a lot of  success on recently. So it’s a shame that we don’t get to play here next year, but I’m sure we’ll see  many, many more brilliant Test matches here. Joe, what was it like being out of the slips for you?  Was there a bit of a freeing up in being able to move around, or how did that differ for you?  Yeah, it was good until I ripped me trousers and me knee open. No, it was good to have that  communication with the bowlers. I think sometimes you find yourself quite distant from things at  slip, but to be on the same page and understand what they’re thinking, them understand how I’m  seeing the game as well, and us to be very aligned on that was important. Like I say, I haven’t  got the experience I had first time around. It was quite easy on occasions to leave Jimmy  and Broady to it. They were very experienced, knew how they were going to operate, and it’s just  different. There are a lot of different things this time around and I think I’m very different  as well. So it was just important, I think, again, with everything around the Test match,  to give as much clarity and simplicity to what we were trying to achieve. We delivered on that  brilliantly. The move to leg slip, can you talk a bit about that as well? Yeah. Worked brilliantly,  didn’t it? It’s nice when a plan comes together. It doesn’t always work like that, but again,  it was the skilful nature of our bowlers to be able to execute it, but also an element of  luck in getting it in exactly the right place. It’s great when a plan comes together. Sometimes,  the one that I enjoyed more was when you put a leg slip in for a different reason and then get the  nick to the keeper, leg side of the ball. There are a number of different things you’re always  trying to work towards, but when your bowlers are skilful enough to deliver on it, that’s the  most rewarding thing. They deserve a huge amount of credit this week because they were excellent.  Joe, given how difficult it’s been for this team over the past few months, both on and off the  field, how important was a statement performance like that this week in terms of moving on and  looking into the future with a bit of positivity? Yeah, I think it’s always important to win Test  matches. You’re playing for England, right? It’s what you set out to do every time you walk out  onto that field. But I think more the fact that we delivered on everything we spoke about. I think  that’s the most pleasing and enjoyable thing about all of it, and it sets us up nicely for the  rest of this series. But it’s understanding that this is one game. There are going to be  other challenges, different things to manage and different opportunities ahead of us, which is  the exciting part. It’s taking the confidence from this and being skilful enough to deal with that  next thing, which will be Lord’s, then building on that, growing it and evolving it over a period  of time. To start like this is excellent, but it’s almost like, right, what does it look like when  we get down to Lord’s and how can we continue a lot of the good stuff we’ve done here? I guess a  start like that helps, doesn’t it? And when you think ahead, maybe [inaudible], right? Yeah, I  think, like I said, it’s not getting too carried away. It’s enjoying what a brilliant performance  it was, seeing guys come into it and have success, with the whole of The Hundred and coming into  a completely different format. Guys had the right attitude, took confidence from it and had  success. It’s been great in so many different ways. Can we now carry that on again? Have you  heard from Stephen Fleming this week? Yeah, every day. What is that, talking to him at the  end of the day’s play? Has he been watching? Yeah, I think he’s kept tabs on things. It’s been  great to have him on the end of the phone and know I can speak to him as much or as little as I  like. It’s great that he’s very invested already in what we’re trying to achieve. There’s been  constant communication with me and Marcus as well. Just on the back of what you said to Rory  about Headingley, when these decisions are made, should home advantage be taken into consideration  a little more? I can’t imagine Australia would play a home Ashes Test and not play at the Gabba.  As a player, it would be nice to have a choice, but obviously this is a slightly different system  here and a different way that things are done. So, yeah, I think I should probably stay in my lane  and understand that it’s someone else’s job to sort out. As a player, you want to play at the  grounds where you have the most success as a team, clearly, and it’s one where we generally do  well and love playing. As a Yorkshireman, I sort of have to say that from birth, so I’m glad  it’s the case. Given Pakistan’s recent struggles, was it a case of just waiting for the bad ball  when you were batting and, when the opposition were bowling, waiting for that bad ball? When you  were bowling at them, was it a case of waiting for them to make a mistake? No, I think it was  about playing the conditions and playing the different situations we found ourselves in.  The game’s never as straightforward as that. It’s always evolving. We had to manage  difficult conditions throughout all of yesterday. There were overcast conditions,  with the lights on for long periods of time, and quite a lot of lateral movement out of the  surface. I thought we were very good at taking our opportunities to score when they came and very  good at absorbing it during the periods when they bowled well. That’s the art of batting. For us  to play in that manner and find the tempo that worked really well on that surface was really  pleasing at the start of the series. As I say, for guys to all have success and almost  still have an element of disappointment yesterday that we all kind of missed out and  didn’t really go on and get a massive score again, it’s a really good place to be as a  team. So I’m thrilled for all of those guys. As mentioned with the ball, Robbo found out what  the length was literally with the first ball of the game and operated brilliantly throughout  the whole Test match. Joe, you’ve played Test cricket against Pakistan for more than a decade  now. Without taking anything away from England, were you slightly surprised by the relative lack  of fight from this particular Pakistan side? I don’t see it like that at all. I’m just really  pleased with our performance and the way that we dealt with things out there. I think we got ahead  of the game and drove the game throughout. I’m really pleased that we continually kept putting  pressure on them in different ways throughout the whole game. That’s all I’m concerned about.  When we find a chance to get ahead in things, can we be good enough to do it? There will  be different times when we’re behind in it, and it’s about how we can wrestle things back in  our favour. But first time out, for us to be as clinical as that and put them under pressure in  different elements of the game for long periods of time like we did, that’s what I’ve reflected  on from this. We know Pakistan have got some wonderful players and they’re a very proud team.  There will be a different set of circumstances, conditions and problems to solve at Lord’s. We’ve  got to be skilful and quick enough to recognise what that looks like and counter that well when  we get our opportunities there. Ollie’s played two games this summer and been Player of the Match in  both. After being outside the side for a couple of years, what difference have you seen in him this  summer? You’ve spoken about him doing fitness work over the last couple of months since his comeback  game at Trent Bridge. Have you seen any difference in him? I thought his performance out there was  brilliant. The fact that he was still as effective in the second innings, having bowled 18 overs or  whatever it was and two pretty long spells, was impressive. An understanding of how he’s going to  operate and what his requirements are in different phases of the game is important. It would be great  to see him pull up really well ahead of Lord’s and back that up again. For him to be effective  as the pitch changed slightly throughout and consistently keep asking difficult questions of  them is a really good sign for us. I’m really pleased for him and I hope he continues  all that great work he’s been doing. Joe, your predecessor was often not that interested  in the World Test Championship, for whatever reason. One of the things that happened over the  last couple of years was slow over-rates causing penalty points and making England drop down the  table. Has there been any thought about addressing that, given also that you’re playing in this game,  and possibly future games, with four seamers, so the over-rate is going to be slower? Is that  something you’ve thought about at all? Yeah, I think it’s also something the ICC should think  about as well. I think if you’re playing in the subcontinent and playing three spinners every  home game, or half your games in those conditions, your over-rate is obviously going to be a lot  more consistently better. That being said, it’s something you’ve always got to try to stay on top  of. It does help when you bowl sides out in under 80 overs and it goes straight back to zero. It  felt like it was easy to manage today when you’re stood next to the bowlers and those conversations  happen more fluidly throughout. Clearly, you want to be competing in those competitions and there  are always things like that you want to brush up on and tidy up. But again, I don’t think it’s  really been too much of a thought of mine over the last little while. It’s been more about trying  to get a performance like that from the group off the bat. It couldn’t have really gone better  for us and I’m really pleased for everyone.
title: ROOT: “STAY IN MY LANE!”  England beat Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs  1st Test
